title: When and How to Pilot: Design Rules for Two-Wave Experiments
abstract: arXiv:2607.16982v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Experimenters often run pilots, but how much a small pilot should shape the main-wave design has no settled answer. This paper shows how noisy pilot evidence should guide treatment assignment probabilities in two-wave experiments. Two canonical rules mark the extremes. Balanced assignment guards against worst cases but ignores evidence that one arm is noisier. Feasible Neyman allocation adapts, but with a finite pilot it can overreact to noise, producing arbitrarily large precision losses. I propose a Conditional Minimax Regret (CMR) rule that minimizes worst-case regret over a finite-sample confidence set for the treatment and control variances. CMR retains balance's worst-case protection with high probability, converges to the Neyman allocation as the pilot grows, and attains the minimax-regret rate up to constants. translated_title: 何时以及如何进行预试验：两波实验的设计规则
translated_abstract: 实验者经常进行预试验，但小型预试验应在多大程度上影响主波设计，尚无定论。本文展示了在双波实验中，有噪声的预试验证据应如何指导治疗分配概率。两个典型规则代表了极端情况。平衡分配能防范最坏情况，但忽略了某一臂噪声更大的证据。可行的奈曼分配会自适应，但在有限预试验下可能对噪声过度反应，导致任意大的精度损失。我提出了一种条件最小最大后悔（CMR）规则，该规则在治疗和控制方差的有限样本置信集上最小化最坏情况后悔。CMR以高概率保留平衡分配的最坏情况保护，随着预试验规模增大而收敛于奈曼分配，并达到常数倍的最小最大后悔率。它扩展到多臂和分层设计，基于四个现场实验的模拟表明，它能避免过度反应。
tldr: 本文提出了一种条件最小最大后悔（CMR）规则，用于在双波实验中平衡预试验证据与最坏情况保护，兼顾稳健性和自适应效率。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a Conditional Minimax Regret (CMR) rule for two-wave experiments, balancing pilot evidence with worst-case protection to achieve both robustness and adaptive efficiency.
